name: Jenkins
description: Protects against destructive Jenkins CLI/API operations like deleting jobs, \ nodes, credentials, or build history.

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-cli-delete-job
destructive_patterns.description: jenkins-cli delete-job deletes Jenkins jobs and can break pipelines.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Jenkins job removes the job configuration, build history, and all \ associated artifacts. Downstream jobs that depend on this job will fail. The \ job definition and history cannot be recovered without backups.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - list-jobs: Review jobs before deletion \ - get-job: Export job XML configuration first \ - Disable the job instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-cli-delete-node
destructive_patterns.description: jenkins-cli delete-node deletes Jenkins nodes and can halt CI.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a Jenkins node (agent) disconnects it from the controller. Jobs \ configured to run on this node will fail or remain pending. Any running builds \ on the node will be aborted immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - get-node: Review node configuration first \ - Take node offline temporarily instead \ - Verify jobs don't require this specific node

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-cli-delete-credentials
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting credentials from Jenkins removes them from the credential store. Jobs \ and pipelines using these credentials will fail authentication. Credential \ values (passwords, tokens, keys) cannot be recovered after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - get-credentials: Review credential metadata first \ - Update credentials instead of deleting \ - Search Jenkinsfiles for credential usage

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-cli-delete-builds
destructive_patterns.description: jenkins-cli delete-builds removes build history and artifacts.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting builds removes build records, console logs, and artifacts for the \ specified build range. This affects audit trails, debugging capabilities, and \ any artifacts needed for deployments. Build history cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - list-jobs: Review job builds first \ - Download artifacts before deletion \ - Use build retention policies instead

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-cli-delete-view
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Jenkins view removes the view configuration. Jobs included in the \ view are not deleted, but the organizational structure is lost. Users relying \ on this view for job navigation will be affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - list-views: Review views before deletion \ - Export view configuration if custom filters are used \ - Create a replacement view before removing

destructive_patterns.name: jenkins-curl-do-delete
destructive_patterns.description: curl POST to Jenkins doDelete endpoints deletes jobs or resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
POSTing to Jenkins doDelete endpoints triggers immediate deletion of jobs, builds, \ or other resources. This bypasses CLI safety checks and directly calls the \ internal deletion API. Resources cannot be recovered without backups.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use jenkins-cli for safer deletion with confirmation \ - GET the resource configuration first for backup \ - Avoid direct API calls for destructive operations
